title: Strategic signal probability buckets and commitment thresholds
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a quantifiable intake and commitment system that converts disparate customer signals into three operational commitment lanes (Fast-track, Standard, Advisory) using probability buckets and explicit acceptance thresholds. The goal is to: (1) formalize why a top-account request should displace roadmap capacity; (2) make commitments auditable and reversible; and (3) provide engineering and sales with a predictable SLA and runway budget tied to measurable triggers.
background: Current intake is ad-hoc: account asks surface through AE/CS, Solutions Eng, and execs without a shared scoring rubric. This causes last-minute scope swaps, missed SLAs, and perception of unfair prioritization. We need a compact, transparent model that balances economic value and product health while preserving PLG-led product integrity.
goals: Define 4 probability buckets (Critical, High, Medium, Low) mapped to commitment lanes
Design a scoring formula combining ARR contribution, integration complexity, regulatory urgency, strategic alignment, churn risk, and delivery cost
Introduce explicit acceptance thresholds and rollback triggers for Fast-track lane
Build an operational runway budget (quarterly token allocation) and expose utilization in Console
Pilot with 5 strategic accounts and measure lead time, churn, and roadmap displacement impact
decision_matrix: Score components and weights: ARR impact (30%), Churn risk delta (25%), Compliance/timebox urgency (15%), Engineering effort (negative weight 20%), Strategic alignment (10%)
Bucket thresholds (example): Critical >= 85, High 70-84, Medium 45-69, Low <45
Fast-track acceptance: requires Critical bucket + exec sponsor + runway tokens available
Rollback triggers: after 2 missed SLOs or >30% scope creep without new runway tokens
Fallback: if runway tokens exhausted, system suggests alternative commitments: staging roadmap item, advisory engagement, or external implementation partner
acceptance_criteria: Scoring engine implemented as a lightweight service (or spreadsheet MVP) that computes bucket for an intake record
Policy doc published with explicit thresholds, required evidence (contracts, NPS, legal requests), and escalation flow
Console dashboard prototype shows runway tokens, active commitments, and historical displacement events
Pilot executed with 5 accounts and retrospective capturing customer satisfaction and internal friction metrics
Rollout playbook including CS/Sales training, intake form template, and PR FAQ is published
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: Draft scoring formula and policy; align with Sales leadership and Legal
Week 2: Build spreadsheet MVP and intake form (Typeform/Google Form) for pilot captures
Week 3-5: Run pilot with 5 accounts; gather evidence and compute buckets; log decisions
Week 6: Build minimal Console view (dashboard card) with runway token counter; link to intake records
Week 7: Publish final policy and handoff to Solutions Eng for production intake automation
Post-pilot: Quarterly review to adjust weights and token budgets tied to company OKRs
metrics: Mean time from intake to decision (target: <= 10 business days for Critical)
% of roadmap slots claimed by committed customer asks (target: <= 25%)
Churn delta among pilot accounts (target: reduction relative to baseline)
Number of rollbacks and root reasons (target: <= 1 per quarter for Fast-track)
Internal satisfaction score among Eng/CS/Sales on fairness and predictability (target: >= 7/10)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-prioritizing paying customers could erode PLG product quality. Mitigation: cap roadmap displacement to runway token budget and require product sign-off for Fast-track items.
Risk: Gaming the scoring inputs by Sales. Mitigation: require objective evidence (contracts, legal notices, telemetry) and cross-functional sign-off on acceptance.
Risk: Engineering capacity fragmentation. Mitigation: define clear engineering SLOs and automated rollback policy tied to telemetry and milestone slippage.
